messages:
alex: quick PSA — profiler (flame id f3a2) shows a perf regression in the streaming + continuous-batching path when load > ~2k concurrent streams. p95 jumps from ~120ms -> ~320ms.

alex: repro steps: local loadtest against region1, model=gptx-8k-quant, seq=1024, token_budget=768, stream=true, concurrency=2000.

maria: can you drop the trace/flamegraph? :eyes:

alex: https://internal.tools/flame/f3a2 (private) — short summary below.

alex: root cause hypothesis: partial-decode flushes are causing kernel re-selection mid-request. when an early flush reduces batch composition, our kernel-chooser flips from small->large kernel (different kernel config), which causes kernel reload + extra KV activity. result: KV miss ratio spikes and work doubles for affected requests.

tao: ack. kernel flip mid-seq is a nasty signal. is KV actually being evicted, or are shard ids changing?

alex: shard ids are stable but we see KV address churn because partial slices change the batch meta used to compute shard assignment. KV miss ratio went 2% -> 18% in the run. also saw a sharp increase in kernel_switch_count in the profiler.

jamie: any quick mitigations we can ship to mitigate user impact?

alex: short-term mitigations that our bench confirms: either lower token_budget or pin kernel selection until end-of-stream. both reduce kernel swaps; tradeoffs differ: lower token_budget stabilizes batch composition, pinning avoids reselect but can run suboptimal kernel for tail tokens.

alex: config we tried that reproduced stable behavior:
```
batching:
  continuous: true
  token_budget: 256
  max_batch_ms: 8
  min_coalesce_size: 2
  partial_decode: conditional
streaming:
  partial_decode_min_tokens: 64
  prefetch_kv: true
  kv_prefetch_heartbeat_ms: 50
```

maria: so lowering token_budget stabilizes batch formation and reduces batch-size variance, which keeps kernel chooser from flipping. makes sense.

tao: what about pinning kernel per-request for streaming?

alex: we tested kernel-pin patch: +8% token-cost (measured) but p95 spike disappears. kernel_switch_count drops ~82%.

jamie: infra-bot, can we schedule a canary with kernel-pin + token_budget=256 on region1? tagging @eng-sre.

infra-bot: @jamie Canary scheduled: canary-2625-kpin at 2625000300 -> region1 (10 nodes).

maria: also recommend enabling a KV prewarm on admission for streaming sessions to avoid cold misses. heartbeat shorter (50ms) helps but watch CPU.

alex: plan for canary: (1) kernel-pin + token_budget=256 (2) enable kv prewarm heartbeat=50ms (3) 1h stable loadtest and collect metrics: kv_miss, kernel_switch_count, p95, token_cost.

tao: assigning myself to dashboards/alerting — will add alert: kernel_switch_rate > 5/min and kv_miss > 10% over 5m.

jamie: i'll own canary rollout and rollback policy.

maria: i'll do post-canary perf diff and regression writeup.

alex: repro command for QA and SRE:
```
./loadtest --target region1 --concurrency 2000 --model gptx-8k --stream --max-tokens 1024 --seed 42
```

maria: sync in 30?

alex: :thumbsup:

infra-bot: deploy-bot: canary started 2625000300.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: canary completed 2625000400 - health OK.

alex: initial canary metrics posted to dashboard: p95 from 320ms -> 150ms, kv_miss 18% -> 3%, kernel_switch_count dropped 82%. token-cost up ~7-9% on canary nodes.

maria: nice work. next step: medium-term we should implement an adaptive token_budget tuner — use first N tokens' distribution to pick budget and/or delay partial-decode until a stability point.

tao: noted. I'll open follow-up issue with experiment plan (auto-tune thresholds + safe fallback).

alex: thanks all. Follow-ups: issue # (TBD), perf writeup from maria, and canary logs uploaded to s3://redwood-perf/canary/2625/

jamie: thanks team — great outcome.

alex: closing loop here, re-run loadtest overnight to sanity-check long-tail behavior.
